title: IDF Drone Strike Kills Hamas Deir al-Balah Battalion Commander Sharif al-Hasanat
detail: An Israeli drone strike hit central Gaza's Deir al-Balah on Saturday, August 22, 2026, killing Sharif al-Hasanat, whom the IDF identified as a company commander in Hamas's Deir al-Balah Battalion. The military said al-Hasanat had been involved in efforts to restore Hamas's underground tunnel infrastructure and posed 'an immediate threat' to Israeli forces, and that it used precision munitions and aerial surveillance to mitigate civilian harm. Palestinian medical sources separately reported one person killed in an Israeli drone strike on a central Gaza home; the IDF said it was looking into those reports. The strike came amid continuing low-level Israeli operations inside Gaza more than ten months after the October 2025 ceasefire, which Turkey, Egypt and Qatar have urged Israel to fully observe.

confidenceReason: IDF statement on the named target corroborated by both Times of Israel and Haaretz; separate Palestinian casualty report from the same strike window is unconfirmed pending IDF review.

title: Turkey Seeks Interpol Red Notice for Netanyahu Over Gaza Flotilla Interception, Alleging Genocide
detail: Turkish Justice Minister Yilmaz Tunc's ministry announced on August 21, 2026 (reported widely August 22) that Turkey had issued an arrest warrant — dated July 14 but disclosed publicly this weekend — for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Israeli official Afek Moskovitch over Israel's May 2026 interception of the Global Sumud Flotilla in international waters en route to Gaza. The warrant, part of a broader case naming 35 individuals, alleges genocide, crimes against humanity and torture, and Ankara is requesting Interpol issue a Red Notice. Netanyahu's office dismissed the move as 'pathetic' and called Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan an 'antisemitic dictator,' vowing to 'act forcefully' against what it described as Turkish attempts to destabilize the region. France, Italy and Australia have separately opened their own judicial proceedings related to the flotilla interception, which triggered a diplomatic crisis in May after images circulated of bound, kneeling detainees.

confidenceReason: Warrant and Interpol Red Notice request confirmed directly by Turkey's Justice Ministry and corroborated by Al Jazeera and Times of Israel; Netanyahu office's response independently quoted by both outlets.
